significance.root_decision: The conjectured formula fails: f(514) ≤ 536 < 537. Take three parts A, B, C of t vertices with every edge between different parts and none inside a part; add one private vertex for each triangle abc, put all private vertices in a clique joined to everything else, and give the edge ab and the edges from each c to its private vertex for (a, b, c) one shared colour, every other edge its own colour. A clique uses at most one vertex of C, so it meets each shared colour at most once, except the full triangle with its own private vertex; this gives a member of the source's class with t³ + 3t vertices for k = t³ + 2, which beats the formula from t = 8 on. A variable-core version gives f(k) ≤ k + 3⌈(k−2)^{1/3}⌉ for every k ≥ 4. Since the source's Lemma 3.3 proves α_{k+2} = f(k), the printed chain is false; together with the source's lower bound (its Lemma 3.10, quoted and not formalized), α_r − r = Θ(r^{1/3}), against the square-root growth the formula predicts. Lean states the source's three properties literally with colours in ℕ (the source's own palette), proves the refutation, the t-family, the every-k bound and that the formula fails for every t ≥ 8, and checks that f(k) ≥ k + 1 for k ≥ 1 and that the rainbow K_{k+1} is not a member.
significance.caveat: The construction is one page and elementary once seen (cross-model reviewer: not routine 0.80; final checker 0.75-0.80). The Lean definition of f fixes the palette to ℕ: a first formalization with an arbitrary palette type was vacuous (the empty palette admits the zero-vertex graph, so f = 0), found and proved by the Lean lane; root fixed the palette to ℕ, which the source states and which gives the same f as any infinite palette. The Θ(r^{1/3}) statement uses the source's Lemma 3.10 for its lower half, quoted, not formalized. The SIAM journal text was not read (403). The Lean was written by GPT-6.1 Sol lanes and finished by a Claude Opus 5.5 lane; because GPT-6.1 Sol hit its usage limit, the final check was by a separate Claude Opus 5.5 lane, the same model family as the packager (the cross-model review is the Opus pre-Lean review of a Sol proof).
